checklist.notes: The set directly practises the manage sense of run, earlier-versus-later past relationships, and consonant-to-vowel linking, then combines those targets in a communicative speaking task.
Controlled form and meaning work precedes interpretation and production, with answer data or an analytic rubric available for every task.
The sequence moves from completion and sentence construction through reading to integrated speaking, followed by a focused Vietnamese-to-English consolidation task.

Instructions, temporal relationships, and intended meaning are explicit; the connected-speech boundary is now separately identified, though its vertical-bar notation still merits a brief learner-facing explanation.
Most items isolate one or two targets, and the harder speaking task limits integration to two concrete constraints with a short two-dimension rubric.
The Vietnamese-to-English item provides targeted cross-linguistic retrieval, while connected-speech noticing is offered without making unsupported claims about all Vietnamese learners.
Four bounded controlled responses plus one concise spoken account are proportionate for a B1.1 consolidation lesson and avoid repetitive padding.

methods: Reviewed the supplied exercise set and audit against their declared project-authored, no-external-payload, and no-external-media evidence.
copyright_originality_check.scope_limitations: No Internet-wide copyright or plagiarism search was performed; this review checked only the supplied artifacts and their declared provenance evidence.

findings.description: The learner-facing meaning of the vertical bar in “run | an” is not explicitly stated, and a vertical bar can visually suggest a pause rather than continuous linking.
findings.recommendation: When rendered, define the bar as a boundary marker with no pause, or model the intended link with an unambiguous notation and spoken example.

limitations: This is an independent AI pedagogical review for development evidence, not human review or release approval.
The review covers only the supplied exercise set and automated audit; it does not independently validate linguistic correctness or perform an Internet-wide originality search.
